messages:
Andre L: FYI billing alert — unexpected GPU hours spike in us-west1 this morning, ~6x baseline. tagging infra.
cost-billing-bot: Alert: High GPU spend detected in project redwood-prod-us-west1 (increase: 5.8x). Top contributor: compute.googleapis.com/instance (a100-80gb) — 4.9k GPU-hours.
Maria P: Oof. Any CPU/GPU autoscale events?
Andre L: scale-bot posted a ton of launches between 04:20-04:27. I pulled the autoscaler logs: see snippet.
Andre L: ```json
{"event":"scale_up","reason":"pending_queue_depth","chosen_pool":"gpu-pool-x","instance_type":"a100-80gb","count":18}
```
Kevin S: Wait gpu-pool-x should be a10g pool. Where did a100 come from?
Samir: Looks like a provisioner template mismatch after the config roll earlier. @Kevin S did the rollout touch pool-template?
Kevin S: I changed the allocation policy to prefer high-memory for long sequences. Did not touch pool-template but I updated label mapping -> maybe a bad regex in selector.
Maria P: I'm seeing nodepool labels: `accelerator=nv` vs expected `accelerator=a10g`. Regex might match 'nv' -> picks anything with 'n'?
Andre L: Also found this in allocator logs: `pool_selector: name =~ /gpu-.*/` then `prefers: accelerator =~ /.*x/` which matched a100-80gb...
Samir: Ugh. So scale-controller picked wrong accelerator family due to overly broad regex in preference.
Kevin S: Immediate mitigation: scale-controller config rollback to previous constraints + drain the a100 nodes. Who wants to take?
Maria P: I'll open a revert PR now and set an emergency policy to cap instance_type to a10g.
Andre L: Can we scale down the a100 nodes gracefully? We have 18 launched, no long-running workloads.
Samir: I'll run:
Samir: ```bash
# cordon then drain cheap
gcloud compute instances list --filter='labels=pool:gpu-pool-x AND cpuPlatform:a100' --format=json | jq '.[].name' | xargs -n1 gcloud compute instances delete --zone=us-west1-b --quiet
```
Kevin S: don't delete until we confirm no jobs. Use drain + node-termination instead.
Samir: ack. I'll cordon + drain, migrate jobs.
cost-billing-bot: Note: since these are a100 preemptibles committed? Billing shows on-demand a100s billed. We should check commitment tags.
Andre L: Action items: 1) Maria revert config (owner Maria) 2) Samir drain and migrate (owner Samir) 3) Kevin add stricter selector + unit tests (owner Kevin) 4) Finance confirm billing refund eligiblity (owner Andre) 5) Alerting: add budget threshold for single-instance-type spend (owner Ops Oncall)
Maria P: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/commit/987abc - rolling back allocator prefs. patch: restrict preference regex to `^a10g(-.*)?$`
Kevin S: I'll add selector tests and a linter for regex in templates.
Andre L: Timeline: aim to fully revert + drains in next 2 hours. Maria ETA 20m.
Ops Oncall: Re budget alert: increased sensitivity, set per-pool 2x baseline. :rotating_light: 
Samir: Drain started 04:55 UTC. Migrating 12/18 tasks.
cost-billing-bot: Billing snapshot (04:00-06:00 UTC): estimated extra = $12,400. Notified Finance.
Finance Bot: Ticket created FIN-3421 for cost investigation.
Maria P: Revert merged at 05:07 UTC, scale-controller rolled back 05:09.
Samir: Drains complete at 05:40, 3 instances needed manual eviction, done.
Kevin S: PR to add regex linter: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/204 - will include unit tests that enumerate instance families.
Andre L: Good postmortem next steps: add template validation in CI, add quota caps for expensive instance types, tag dedicated commit pools with commitment_id so billing auto-maps.
Ops Oncall: Filing incident doc in /postmortems. Assign small blameless postmortem.
Maria P: thx all. cc @Finance Team for refund pursuit.
Andre L: moving to follow-ups channel. :thumbsup:
